text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a central repository. The heart of CI is the automated build, which happens every time new code is pushed. This build compiles the software and automatically runs a suite of tests. By doing this, the team catches issues early, often within minutes of a change being made. A CI pipeline orchestrates this process, from checking out the code to running tests and reporting results. This constant feedback loop means problems are fixed quickly, reducing the time spent debugging later and making the entire development process smoother and more reliable.
